source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
PowerHouse ABX-1 in Ashburn, Virginia publishes one technical figure: 265,850 square feet of technical space. Megawatt capacity is not published on the operator's spec page, so no translation into racks or accelerators is possible without inventing a number this site does not have. The absence of a published power figure is itself meaningful, because it prevents any direct comparison of this campus's AI-readiness against facilities where load capacity is stated.

Virginia hosts 326 mapped facilities, of which only 19 publish a megawatt figure. Those 19 facilities together account for 1,326 MW of published IT capacity. This campus ranks twentieth by published megawatts, which in practice means it falls outside the 19 facilities that contribute to that state total, because no wattage figure is on record here. Ashburn is the densest data center market in that state, so the square footage alone confirms this is a substantial physical footprint, but physical size and power capacity are not the same thing.

No certifications are listed in the published specifications, so no statement about what workloads the campus is qualified to host can be made. A reader evaluating this campus for AI deployment needs at minimum a published IT load figure and a power-delivery tier before drawing conclusions. Until PowerHouse publishes those numbers, this facility is a large building in the world's busiest data center corridor whose relevance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from operator-published data alone.
